name: Dragonfly
tagline: A multi-threaded, shared-nothing in-memory store that speaks Redis and Memcached on one big box.
description: Dragonfly reimplements the Redis and Memcached APIs on a shared-nothing, thread-per-core architecture, so a single process can use dozens of cores instead of needing a Redis Cluster of many shards. Its dashtable layout and fork-free snapshotting also cut memory overhead and avoid the copy-on-write spikes that make Redis BGSAVE painful. It is a strong fit for teams that want to vertically scale a Redis workload on large instances. Version 2.0 shipped in September 2026, still under BSL 1.1, which forbids offering it as a competing managed service.

pricing.notes: Free to self-host under BSL; Dragonfly Cloud and Dragonfly Enterprise are paid.

scale.notes: Designed to scale up to hundreds of GB and millions of ops/s per node; cluster mode and Dragonfly Swarm add horizontal scaling.

strengths: Thread-per-core design scales one instance across many cores without cluster sharding
Fork-free snapshots avoid Redis-style memory spikes during persistence
Lower per-key memory overhead than Redis for many workloads
Speaks both RESP and Memcached, easing consolidation of two cache tiers
Built-in search and JSON commands compatible with RediSearch/RedisJSON clients
weaknesses: BSL 1.1 license restricts offering it as a managed service
Some Redis commands and module behaviours differ or are missing
Smaller ecosystem and fewer managed options than Redis/Valkey
Still bounded by the RAM of the machines you run
useCases: Consolidating many Redis shards onto fewer large instances
Replacing Memcached and Redis with one engine
notIdealFor: Vendors building a hosted Redis-compatible service
Workloads depending on niche Redis modules
